sense.text:
Today’s topic is pride and divine judgment, and we open with pride. “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” That is what the Bible calls pride.

Today’s society calls pride having confidence in something: I have great pride in who I am. That is not the way the Bible uses the word. The Bible uses pride in a negative context: when you stop keeping the commandments, when you turn away from the laws of God.

You have Israelites that say we have pride because we don’t listen to them. That is not the pride the Bible is talking about. It doesn’t say when our heart is turned away from you, brother online. I don’t want to listen to your doctrine. I don’t have pride, I just don’t want to listen to you. Who are you? Where’d you come from? You just popped out of your mama’s behind last week.

“For pride is the beginning of sin”: sin is breaking God’s laws. “And he that hath it shall pour out abomination.” We know Esau’s abominations, but here are some Israelite abominations. When you hear Israelites say reject the teachings of Christ, that’s an abomination. When you hear Israelites say reject the teachings of the Apostle Paul, that’s an abomination. When you hear Israelites say let’s celebrate Thanksgiving and call it Yahawashi day, that is an abomination. When they say women can dress like men, that’s an abomination; when they say men can dress like women, that’s an abomination.

If you’re in the midst of sin you’re going to pour out all manner of filthiness out of your mouth, and it’s going to go against the scriptures. When you hear Israelites say one wife, to hell with that, I’m going to have multiple girlfriends regardless of what Christ said, that’s pouring out abomination. That’s pride, because you’ll read it: one wife in the Bible until the kingdom come. No, no, I need it now, I want it, I needs it, I got to have it.

“And therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.” That’s what happened to us as a nation, as a people. You don’t want to listen; all strange doctrines, get the hell out of here. Like the hexagram God gave David, that six-pointed star: what scripture says that? That’s an abomination.

“And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end”: no end of making many books about God. There’s a man, Billy Carson, on all the top podcasts, and nobody could challenge him on the crap he says, because he’s reading fraudulent documents. Brothers, as long as we stay in the Bible we good. It’s when you go outside the Bible that people like this start talking nonsense, and people think he makes sense but it makes no sense. He has all these books.

Back in the late 80s and early 90s there was another one who did all these crazy, stupid books just like this. It’s what I always call jailhouse talk: the way these people talk is so nonsensical, it’s like they had nothing better to do but sit in jail for years and make stupid stuff up, come out of jail and teach it to dumb black people, and dumb black people do what dumb black people do: follow dumb black people. An Edomite tore this dude up last week. All these Afrocentric, Egyptology nonsense, the Anunnaki and scientists in the middle of the earth: it’s ridiculous, and you have dumb Israelites going on these dumb shows talking dumb stuff with no solution for the black community, no solutions at all and no Bible. One used to say the black woman could have a baby without a man, using just a gland, and dumb black men and dumb black women going yeah, yeah. How does she do it? Where’s the first woman that did this thing? Where’s the children that come from that? Pop out the baby right now, I want to see it. It makes no sense, but they be clapping and donating money.

This man referenced the Gilgamesh epic: oh yeah, there’s a story of the flood, and it talks about the goddess Easter, and she had a bull in heaven that came down. That’s Baal and Easter, Ishtar. This is foolishness, idolatry. They say it’s the oldest record: shut the hell up, there’s nothing older than in the beginning. You can’t get around that; there’s nothing before that. Then the 42 negative confessions, and Moses copied it from the Egyptian writings: just shut up. People like this will make books every week on foolishness and stupidity.

There’s an Edomite who goes to school, his whole thing is theology and religion, he goes with archaeologists and does research, and everybody’s praising him. He used to say Christmas was pagan; now he says through research he found out it is very biblical. You lost me there, Edomite: Christmas is not biblical. Watch these people; they are slick. Their soul is not upright in them.

“And much study is a weariness of the flesh.” Studying all the books, studying all these stupid books, is a waste of time. Weariness of the flesh means you’re wasting your time, because these books are taking you away from the one true living God.

“Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.” Verse 13 is the key to everything. When y’all start reading all these other books with their opinions about God, it takes you away. Back at the old school when the split happened there was a book that said the Israelites ruled the ancient Egyptians as the Hyksos empire. It made no sense, because the Bible says we were slaves, and you had Israelites teaching that the Israelites ruled Egypt for centuries. That makes no biblical sense. This is what the Bible is talking about: you’re so busy in verse 12 you miss verse 13.

“For God shall bring every work into judgment”: everything you do shall be judged, “with every secret thing”: every secret thing you do at night when you think nobody’s watching, “whether it be good, or whether it be evil.”

precepts.why: “For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.” We shall all appear before the judgment seat of Christ. That’s the same thing Solomon told us in Ecclesiastes 12:14: God shall bring every work into judgment, every secret thing, whether it be good or evil.

sense.text: “For many great miseries shall be done to them that in the latter time shall dwell in the world”: there’s going to be a lot of miseries in these last days. “Because they have walked in great pride.” People on this earth today walk in great pride, and certain amongst our own people walk in great, great pride, and the pride is going against God’s laws. When our people go to what they call church, that’s great pride. Transgenderism and all that filth: abominations, all of them. All of them have left the living God and all of them shall be judged. All of this is filth, and the Most High is going to bring judgment on their behind. Judgment is coming.

“But understand thou for thyself”: y’all better learn this Bible for yourselves. Although we’re teaching it to you, you better each learn to absorb it, take it in and understand it for yourselves. “And seek out the glory for such as be like thee”: we’re looking for the elect, looking for men and women that truly believe. That’s what we’re doing; that’s the elect we’re looking for.

“Then said Isaiah to Hezekiah, Hear the word of the Lord of hosts: Behold, the days come, that all that is in thine house, and that which thy fathers have laid up in store until this day, shall be carried to Babylon: nothing shall be left, saith the Lord.” Isaiah is prophesying about the Babylonian captivity.

“And of thy sons that shall issue from thee, which thou shalt beget”: and he had many sons. “Shall they take away; and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.” Your sons that shall be taken away and gone into captivity shall become eunuchs. A eunuch is when they cut your meat off; you can’t have no more babies ever. Damn, you ain’t got no rod, it’s gone; down there is mutilated.

“Then said Hezekiah to Isaiah, Good is the word of the Lord which thou hast spoken. He said moreover, For there shall be peace and truth in my days.” So although there was peace and truth in Hezekiah’s days, the prophecy was that Babylon was going to come take his sons and make them eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.

precepts.why:
Daniel 1 is the fulfillment of that. “In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah came Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon unto Jerusalem, and besieged it. And the Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, with part of the vessels of the house of God”, and he carried them into the land of Shinar and “brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god.”

Then the king spake unto Ashpenaz, “the master of his eunuchs”: there is Isaiah’s prophecy coming to pass. He was to bring “certain of the children of Israel, and of the king’s seed, and of the princes”: Hezekiah’s seed. “Children in whom was no blemish”: no pimples, no hyperpigmentation; that skin was what they call ruddy, nice. “But well favoured, and skilful in all wisdom, and cunning in knowledge, and understanding science, and such as had ability in them to stand in the king’s palace, and whom they might teach the learning and the tongue of the Chaldeans”: they had to learn a whole new language too.

The king appointed them “a daily provision of the king’s meat, and of the wine which he drank: so nourishing them three years, that at the end thereof they might stand before the king.” Among these were of the children of Judah, Daniel and the others. We never called them by the Hebrew names we read in verse 6; everybody knows them as Shadrach and the others, and those are their slave names. Shake those names.

sense.text: Nebuchadnezzar was in power, then he died, and some time later his grandson took over. “Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords, and drank wine before the thousand.” He commanded to bring “the golden and silver vessels which his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem”; next to the word father there is a note that says grandfather.

They brought the golden vessels of the house of God, and the king, his princes, his wives and his concubines “drank in them.” They were mocking the vessels that were stolen from the temple of the Lord. “They drank wine, and praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of stone.”

“In the same hour came forth fingers of a man’s hand, and wrote over against the candlestick upon the plaister of the wall of the king’s palace: and the king saw the part of the hand that wrote.” He saw the hand writing on the wall. “Then the king’s countenance was changed, and his thoughts troubled him, so that the joints of his loins were loosed”: he got real scared. “And his knees smote one against another”: that’s great fear. When you see a hand appear out of nowhere and just start writing on the walls, what the hell is this? He’s terrified.

He cried aloud for “the astrologers, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers”, promising that whoever could read the writing should be clothed with scarlet, have a chain of gold about his neck, “and shall be the third ruler in the kingdom.” Then came in all the king’s wise men, and none of the astrologers could interpret the writing on the wall. Y’all can read the rest on your own; the children have read this already in Sabbath class.

“There is a man in thy kingdom, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods”: there’s a man in your kingdom, Belshazzar, who has the spirit of the holy gods. “Light and understanding and wisdom, like the wisdom of the gods, was found in him”: all that we read in chapter one. Nebuchadnezzar made him master of the magicians, astrologers, Chaldeans and soothsayers.

“Forasmuch as an excellent spirit, and knowledge, and understanding, interpreting of dreams, and shewing of hard sentences, and dissolving of doubts”: when Daniel spoke, that is what they were making reference to. He dissolved all doubts; he was a dissolver of doubts when he spoke. “Now let Daniel be called, and he will shew the interpretation.”

Now they call Daniel. Remember Daniel is old now; they were 70 years in Babylon, so he’s up in age. “Art thou that Daniel, which art of the children of the captivity of Judah, whom the king my father brought out of Jewry?”

“I have even heard of thee, that the spirit of the gods is in thee, and that light and understanding and excellent wisdom is found in thee.” See what it says in verse 14, the spirit of the gods is in thee, and remember verse 11, a man in whom is “the spirit of the holy gods.” What they’re making reference to is what the scriptures call the Holy Spirit, what the Hebrew community calls the ruach. The holy spirit is the spirit of truth; that’s what the Babylonians called the spirit of the holy gods.

precepts.why:
“If ye love me, keep my commandments.” That is the stipulation for getting the spirit, the Holy Spirit. “And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth.” So the holy spirit is the spirit of truth; that’s what the Babylonians called the spirit of the holy gods in Daniel 5.

“Whom the world cannot receive”: the world can’t receive the Holy Spirit, “because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him.” Y’all be looking at these people on TV that claim to have the Holy Spirit, but they don’t keep no commandments; they don’t have the Holy Spirit. All that rolling, I’m slain in the spirit, rolling on the floor foaming at the mouth: that’s not the Holy Spirit. That’s a fornicating demon. Foaming at the mouth, doing back flips in church: the hell is this?

“But ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you”: he’s telling you who the holy spirit is. Verse 18 seals the deal, and you have to stress the right word: “I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.” He’s telling you he’s the holy spirit. It’s not Elijah Muhammad, it’s not Dr York, it’s not Muhammad. Christ is telling you, I am the Holy Spirit, I will come to you. I don’t see how people could be so damn dumb.

“But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things.” When you receive the Holy Ghost, the Holy Spirit, number one, the stipulation is you must be keeping the commandments (verse 15). Then he shall teach you all things, “and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.”

So the Holy Spirit would teach us about the speakings and sayings of Christ: how the Israelites would fall and go into captivity, and then be resurrected in the last days and wake up again. How come no church that claims to have the Holy Spirit knows that? They don’t know it, because you got to keep the commandments. A preacher on TV waves his dirty jacket, a jacket that cost probably $2,000, and people fall out and say I’m slain in the spirit. The hell is this? He don’t do it in the hospital.

Verse 23 is the point. “How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity?” Reading all those stupid books by that guy Carson: you simple for that. “And the scorners delight in their scorning”: there’s no God, there’s no Christ; they delight in scorning. “And fools hate knowledge”: fools hate God’s laws.

“Turn you at my reproof”: God’s reproof is his laws, so turn you at my reproof means keep God’s laws. And what will God do for us if we turn at his reproof? “Behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.” That’s John 14:15, the same thing Christ said: keep my commandments and I will pray the Father, and you shall receive the Holy Spirit. Turn at my reproof and I will pour out my spirit unto you. It’s saying the same thing; that is the spirit that was in Daniel.

Daniel saw dreams and was able to interpret things, and the scriptures talk about that in these last days. When you read Joel 2, do not start at verse 28; always start at verse 27. Christians don’t like that, because they like to make Joel 2:28 all inclusive, for all races of people, but it’s not talking about all races of people.

“And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else.” Christians hate that verse. So you mean he’s not the god of the Chinese? No. He’s not the god of the white man? No. Not the god of the Arabs? No. He’s nobody else’s God but our God. “And my people shall never be ashamed.”

“I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh”: Christians highlight all flesh and say see, everybody. No, dummy, verse 27 already cleared the thought: it’s talking about the Israelites. That spirit is the same spirit Daniel had, the same spirit Christ was talking about, the same spirit we rolling in. “And your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions: And also upon the servants”: some brothers and sisters had servants and will have servants; you have employees, workers. “And upon the handmaids in those days will I pour out my spirit”: that’s the Holy Spirit.

Although this occurred in the book of Acts chapter two, from verse 30 down is really talking about these last days. “And I will shew wonders in the heavens and in the earth, blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke”: destruction. “The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and the terrible day of the Lord come.” So before the second coming the Lord said, I’m going to pour out my spirit upon all flesh, meaning all the flesh of the Israelites.

“Whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered”, and here’s the answer: “for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance.” Deliverance is not for all races on the planet earth. “And in the remnant whom the Lord shall call”: that’s still Israel. We all want that Holy Spirit; we want the Lord to pour his spirit out upon us.

sense.text:
We all want that Holy Spirit; we want the Lord to pour His Spirit out upon us. Here they are having a conversation with Daniel, and he’s an old man now. “I have even heard of thee, that the spirit of the gods is in thee, and that light and understanding and excellent wisdom is found in thee.” See that light and understanding there.

That same spirit that was on Daniel is to be on us.

precepts.why: Remember what Christ said: “Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.” So when we come into this truth we are the light. We have that spirit; the spirit of the holy God is on us, and we are that light of the world, the same light and understanding that was found in Daniel.

“But call to remembrance the former days, in which, after ye were illuminated”: that is the same illumination as what Daniel had. “Ye endured a great fight of afflictions”: so we must endure a great fight of afflictions soon to come.

“But the love of the Lord passeth all things for illumination: he that holdeth it, whereto shall he be likened?” You can’t compare a man or a woman who is holding the illumination of the Lord, who has the love of the Lord on them.

“Turn thee, O Jacob”: we are Jacob. “And take hold of it: walk in the presence of the light thereof, that thou mayest be illuminated.” That is the light and understanding that was found in Daniel, held out to Jacob.

sense.text: “But they could not shew the interpretation of the thing”, because the writing was in ancient Hebrew. It wasn’t Aramaic; it was in the pure tongue they call the king’s tongue, the king’s language, which was the ancient Hebrew.

“And I have heard of thee, that thou canst make interpretations, and dissolve doubts”. Remember when Daniel came, they had to teach him a new language; in chapter one it says they had to teach him their language. So nobody knew his language.
“Let thy gifts be to thyself”: keep your gifts, I don’t need your gifts. “And give thy rewards to another”: give your rewards to somebody else.
“O thou king, the most high God gave Nebuchadnezzar thy father a kingdom, and majesty, and glory, and honour”. Now he’s reading the writing: he’s looking at the wall as he’s talking.
“All people, nations, and languages, trembled and feared before him”: he conquered everybody.

“But when his heart was lifted up, and his mind hardened in pride”. In what? In pride. King Nebuchadnezzar had great pride, and he parted from the one true God. Daniel was trying to teach him and show him about the Living God, and he said, I don’t want to hear that.

“Till he knew that the most high God ruled in the kingdom of men”: he had to acknowledge the one true God. “And that he appointeth over it whomsoever he will.” Nebuchadnezzar had to realize what Daniel was trying to show him: you are only ruling because the one true God allowed you to rule. In his mind, his pride said no, I’m ruling because I’m all powerful.

precepts.why:
Herod did the same thing. “Herod was highly displeased with them of Tyre and Sidon”: that’s in Lebanon. They “desired peace; because their country was nourished by the king’s country”: there was a huge trade of imports and exports of food between Herod’s kingdom and Tyre and Sidon.

“Upon a set day Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne, and made an oration unto them”: he gave a great BS speech. “And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man.” Watch this: “And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him”. Why? “Because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost.” See that: pride, pride, pride. Just like Nebuchadnezzar.

This is where it was told to Nebuchadnezzar: “This matter is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the holy ones: to the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men”. Man does not want to acknowledge that the Most High rules this planet. Man wants to think he does things of his own accord; that’s called pride.

“And giveth it to whomsoever he will”: God gives the kingdom to whomsoever he will. “And setteth up over it the basest of men.” Base is the root word of basement: the bottom level, the lowest you can go. So God said, I set the lowest of the nations over this world. You think the white man is so high and mighty; God says no, those are base people. A people who create a weapon to destroy themselves, a base people. A people who create fake food to kill the population, a base people.

sense.text: “And thou his son, O Belshazzar, hast not humbled thine heart, though thou knewest all this”: he didn’t humble his heart though he knew all that Daniel just said. He didn’t humble himself.

“They have brought the vessels of his house before thee”: they brought the vessels of the house of the Lord in mockery. While Daniel is talking he’s looking at the ancient Hebrew writing on the wall.

“And the God in whose hand thy breath is, and whose are all thy ways, hast thou not glorified”. That’s why we went to Wisdom of Solomon: our breath is in God’s hand.
“MENE; God hath numbered thy kingdom, and finished it.” They fell around 529; that’s when the Medes and Persians came in and destroyed Babylon.
“TEKEL; Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting”: found lacking.
“Thy kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians.” That is what Daniel was speaking of: the Persians and Medes were going to come and destroy the kingdom.
“In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain”: he was killed, murdered, slain.

“And Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old”: 62.

We got to make sure that we don’t have that spirit of pride in us. Always, in all things, acknowledge the one true God.

precepts.why:
Your life was lent to you. “He maketh a vain god of the same clay, even he which a little before was made of earth himself, and within a little while after returneth to the same”: you return back to the earth out of which you were taken, “when his life which was lent him shall be demanded.”

Our lives are not our own. The life we’re living now was loaned to us, lent to us. You think you’re alive because your mama had you? No: the fact that you’re breathing, that’s a loan; God is lending you that. And it’s going to be demanded: that breath you’re taking right now will be demanded one day. We must all acknowledge that. That is the God in whose hand thy breath is, whom Belshazzar did not glorify.

This goes for all of us, because many brothers and sisters do this. “Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow.” We don’t know what tomorrow is going to bring. “For what is your life? It is even a vapour”: it’s a smoke, “that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.” Here today, gone tomorrow.

“For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.” That’s what we got to start saying. Not, hey, tomorrow I’m going to do this, I’m going to do that. No, that’s pride: you don’t know that God’s going to give you that life tomorrow.

“But now ye rejoice in your boastings: all such rejoicing is evil.” James is saying it’s evil when you say what you’re going to do tomorrow, and your life is not even your own. “Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.” If you know the right things to say and you choose not to say them, it is sin to you.

That’s something we often slip with the tongue. We got to catch ourselves and say, Lord’s will, if life lasts and the Lord allows me, I’ll do this, that and the other. We must always give God the glory.

sense.text:
“For Christ sent me not to baptize”: meaning run around doing water baptisms. Christ did not send me to go around dipping people in water. You always get people that come into school asking, can you dip me in water, like the water is a quick fix. The water ain’t doing nothing for you, sister, brother; it’s just making you wet. They were arguing about baptism at first here, and Paul had to set the record straight.

“But to preach the gospel”: that’s why we’re sent, to preach the gospel. Hey, dip me in some water, brother? No, I ain’t dipping you in the water. Give me a bottle of water, pour it on your head: how about that, you good now?

“Not with wisdom of words”: meaning man’s wisdom. “Lest the cross of Christ should be made of none effect”: lest you take away from the cross of Christ the glory. The honor must be Christ’s.

You hear brothers say, don’t say Christ, it’s evil. Christ and Messiah are the same word: Christ is Greek, Messiah is Hebrew, and they both mean in English anointed. What is wrong with black people? You can’t say it in Greek, it’s evil? Are you stupid? One of those stupid books, said to be an old book, said that Jesus was Christ but not the Messiah, but those are the same words. That shows the fraudulence of those stupid books, and people can’t figure out the meanings of words. Stop being stupid; silly rabbit, tricks are for kids.

“For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness”: to them that are destined to perish it is foolishness. They didn’t want to hear how Christ died on the cross for the nation of Israel. “But unto us which are saved”: destined to be saved, “it is the power of God.” The sacrifice of Christ is the power of God. It brings us back to the covenant of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; that’s the adoption of sons again.

“I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent.” The wise and prudent at that time was Rome. In this time here it’s America: everybody looks to the all American white man for wisdom and prudence, just like back then they looked to Rome for all knowledge and wisdom. God said, I’m going to destroy all that.

“Where is the wise? where is the scribe? where is the disputer of this world?” Where’s the man or woman that’s going to argue on its behalf? Back then it was Rome; today it’s America. You want to stand up and say God bless America? Are you kidding me? I remember the dude who said if it wasn’t for the greatness of the white man we would eat you. Shut the hell up, negro. We had to shut this dude down quick, because a stupid spirit will carry; it’ll go from head to head. Everybody stop being stupid.

“Hath not God made foolish the wisdom of this world?”

“For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God”: with all the world’s wisdom, all the technological advancements, they still don’t know the one true God. “It pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.” That’s how the Lord’s going to save us; that’s how he’s saving us, through preaching the word. Preaching means prophesying.

“For the Jews require a sign”: they always wanted a sign, give us a sign so that we know you are the Son of God. “And the Greeks seek after wisdom”: the Greeks is still talking about the Israelites. The Jews is the kingdom of Judah; the Greeks is making reference to the northern kingdom, and remnants of Judah too.
“But we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews a stumblingblock, and unto the Greeks foolishness”.

precepts.why:
People always get mad about the baptism thing, but we got to read it. I’ve been water baptized like seven times, every church my mama took us to, and came out more wicked than the first time we went in.

“The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us”: the apostle Peter says yes, baptism does save you, but “not the putting away of the filth of the flesh”. Water baptism is what puts away the filth of the flesh, and he’s saying I’m not talking about that kind of baptism. Baptism with water doesn’t save you; it just makes you wet; it was just symbolic.

“But the answer of a good conscience toward God”: keeping the commandments. And what else? “By the resurrection of Jesus Christ”. What gives us a good conscience is keeping the commandments and believing in Jesus Christ, that resurrection. That’s the baptism that saves us, not the water. You can get dipped in water every morning and you’re still wicked as hell. That’s why Christ sent Paul not to baptize but to preach the gospel.

This is the disputer of this world. You’re on the street and somebody’s talking a whole lot of nothing, blah blah blah, using words they just read in the dictionary two days ago and were waiting for an opportunity to use on you. “Produce your cause, saith the Lord; bring forth your strong reasons, saith the King of Jacob.” Okay, what do you say, brother? What are you talking about? And he’s talking about all that crap.

“Let them bring them forth, and shew us what shall happen”: you got to pause them and say, prophesy to us; with all that you said, what is going to happen? “Let them shew the former things”: tell us about the former things. Why did we as a people go into slavery? Riddle me that, Batman. “What they be, that we may consider them”: that we may consider what you’re saying to be true, “and know the latter end of them”. “Or declare us things for to come”: prophesy about the United States of America, what’s going to happen. What’s going to happen in Syria? You see what’s happening in Syria, it’s getting blown the hell up; we were just talking about that. What’s going to happen to China? “Shew the things that are to come hereafter, that we may know that ye are gods”: that we may know that the religion you’re in is the way of the true God.

These men and these women couldn’t tell you what happened in the past, they can’t tell you why we’re in this current situation, and they cannot tell you the future. But the Bible can; the Bible has the answers to all that. And you got to have the spirit of the holy God on you in order to understand what it says. In the Quran there’s nothing: the Quran can’t tell you nothing that happened to black people or Latin people, can’t tell you who you were in the past, can’t tell you why you wound up here, and the Quran sure as hell ain’t going to tell you the future. The Bible talks about what’s going to happen to Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Iran, America, China. The Quran don’t do none of that; it’s a waste of time.

“Yea, do good, or do evil, that we may be dismayed, and behold it together”: shock us with your endowed wisdom. “Behold, ye are of nothing”: brother, I’m going to stop you there, because your religion is garbage. All that Quran stuff you’re talking about is BS; all that Egyptology, it’s all garbage. “And your work of nought”: meaning nothing. “An abomination is he that chooseth you”: anybody that chooses your religion is an abomination. You chose seven dead men, brother: abomination. You chose Islam: abomination. You chose Buddhism: abomination. You chose Roman Catholicism: abomination. The Bible got the answer right there. That is how God has made foolish the wisdom of this world.

“Lo, thy sons come”: that’s us. “Whom thou sentest away”: we were sent away into captivity. “They come gathered together from the east to the west”: we get gathered together from the east to the west. How? “By the word of the Holy One”. That’s the same thing Paul was saying: that’s how he’s going to save us, through the foolishness of preaching. “Rejoicing in the glory of God.”

sense.text:
Moses did not stutter. Stop saying it. This is the verse they use to say Moses was a stutterer: “O my Lord, I am not eloquent”. You know how somebody can talk but they’re not an eloquent speaker. “But I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.”

Moses was raised in the house of Pharaoh. He knew the Egyptian tongue perfectly, but in the Hebrew language he was slow of tongue, the way you just know a few good words, like we’ve got broken Spanish. Slow of speech is not a stutter.

precepts.why:
Here’s the evidence. “In which time Moses was born, and was exceeding fair, and nourished up in his father’s house three months: And when he was cast out, Pharaoh’s daughter took him up, and nourished him for her own son.”

Then it comes: “And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds.” Mighty in words. A man mighty in words was not a stutterer. It didn’t happen; stop saying that. His slowness of speech in Exodus 4:10 was in the Hebrew tongue, because he was brought up in Pharaoh’s house learning the wisdom of the Egyptians.

“By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.”

The same Moses raised as the son of Pharaoh’s daughter turned from that house and chose the people of God. That clears it up for the ones who are new and came in with those thoughts about a stuttering Moses.

sense.text:
“But we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews a stumblingblock”: the Jews are those Israelites raised up under the laws of Moses, speaking Hebrew. “And unto the Greeks foolishness”: the Greeks are the other group of Israelites, raised under Greek customs, speaking Greek and learning Greek.

The Greeks in the New Testament are Greek-speaking Jews. The Encyclopedia of the Diaspora, a secondary source after the Bible, shows it: in the Hellenistic period, the Greek period, the Jews in the West, the Greek-speaking Mediterranean world, wrote and spoke only Greek, while in the East, where Israel was, Hebrew and Aramaic prevailed, though even there some communities spoke Greek, as you read in the book of Acts. Their religious life, the reading of the Torah and prayer, was carried on in Greek; the Torah was translated into Greek in the third century BCE, and the sages allowed an authorized translation so those scattered Israelites would not be lost, just like a lot of us now only speak English. That is why the New Testament was written in both Hebrew and Greek.

The center of learning in the land was out of reach of that Greek diaspora except for those like Paul, who made the effort to leave their Greek-speaking abode and come and learn in the land of Israel. Paul was born in what is Turkey today, his family had money, and they sent him to learn. The people Paul went to were Jews. He was not going to all other races teaching them; he was teaching the Israelites scattered. This is not even gone over in the churches, and it would help you immensely if you had the Apocrypha with books like this. Tell some Christians this and they cry ‘heresy’; they get offended, simple as hell. All right bro, go stay in your stupidity.

“But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks”: both Jews and Greeks, that’s the two kingdoms coming back. “Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God”: Christ is the power of God and Christ is the wisdom of God.
“The foolishness of God is wiser than men”, wiser than any man, “and the weakness of God is stronger than men.”

“For ye see your calling, brethren”: we have to understand that we have all been called into this truth by the Lord. This is a great and high calling. ‘Many are called but few are chosen.’ This is how important it is.

“How that not many wise men after the flesh”: these are what the world calls wise men, Booker T. Washington, James Baldwin, Marcus Garvey, Frederick Douglass, Malcolm X, Martin Luther King. “Not many mighty”: the mighty men, excellent physical specimens, athletes, Floyd Mayweather, Muhammad Ali, Jordan, Tyson, LeBron. “Not many noble”: the Nobel Peace Prize winners, Desmond Tutu, Patrice Lumumba, Colin Powell, Kofi Annan, Nelson Mandela, Barack Obama. Not many of these are called.

precepts.why:
To understand the Greeks, go to the Greek times. This is the part missing from the canonized King James Bible: they removed the books of the Apocrypha, which give you the history of the Greek captivity.

“Now such was the height of Greek fashions, and increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest; That the priests had no courage to serve any more at the altar”. Because of the Greek fashions the priests, the Levites, did not want to serve anymore. “But despising the temple”, they started to hate the temple of God, “and neglecting the sacrifices, hastened to be partakers of the unlawful allowance in the place of exercise, after the game of Discus called them forth”.

The discus is the game they throw today, like a frisbee: the Olympic Games. All of this comes from the Greeks. Their frescos and their archaeological finds show the discus and the Greek games of old, so what you see today in the Olympics is the same exact thing.

“Not setting by the honours of their fathers, but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all.” Back then, just like today, many of our people want to be like the white man, live in white society, and conduct ourselves like white folks. That is what our people were doing back then; this is the history.

“By reason whereof sore calamity came upon them: for they had them to be their enemies and avengers”. The Greeks were our enemies and we wanted them to avenge us. Makes no damn sense. “Whose custom they followed so earnestly”: we followed Greek customs so earnestly, “and unto whom they desired to be like in all things.” It is just like today: Greek fraternities, Greek this, Alpha Beta Kappa, all that crap. The same mentality. That is the Greeks of 1 Corinthians 1:23: Israelites who took on Greek customs.

“I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you that ye walk worthy of the vocation wherewith ye are called”. It ain’t vacation, it’s vocation: a strong feeling of suitability for a particular career or occupation; a person’s employment or main occupation, especially regarded as particularly worthy and requiring great dedication.

So our career, our occupation, brothers and sisters, is this Bible. It’s not ‘I’m going to school to be a doctor, a lawyer.’ This truth is our occupation, this is our vocation, and we have to give great dedication to it. Not that stuff you’re learning out there. That’s all well and good, and it’s not being knocked, but let this be first. That is the calling of 1 Corinthians 1:26.

“Thus saith the Lord, Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom”. Don’t let a wise brother glory in his wisdom. Some of you go to school all your life and you glory. Mama used to say, the smarter you are the stupider you get, because you start to disregard the Bible. When you are indoctrinated in Esau’s school system it hardens you against the word of God and makes you think you are something when you’re nothing.

Nobody say Bishop said don’t go to school; that is not what was said. You’ve got to work, you’ve got to eat, you’ve got to live: go to school, get an education, don’t be a dummy. But the Bible is first, and the wisdom of this Bible is greater than that in the school system.

“Neither let the mighty man glory in his might”: don’t let you strong brothers glory in yourselves. It’s a sad story with Muhammad Ali, mighty, and his final outcome with the Parkinson’s. The Most High says, all that pride you got, I’mma take you down. There’s a fight on YouTube where a big man was dancing around playing, and the Jake, a skinny guy, opened with one knee to the forehead and took the mighty dude out instantly. He was acting like he was going to win and he lost. The Most High can take you out just like that.

“Let not the rich man glory in his riches: But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me”. That is what we’ve got to glory in: that we know the Lord and understand the scriptures. That and only that, nothing else. “That I am the Lord which exercise lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, saith the Lord.”

The world’s wise, mighty and noble of 1 Corinthians 1:26 are the very ones the Lord says not to glory in.

sense.text: “Unto certain which trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised others”. People who think they are so holy can’t be stood. Go to these Christian churches and a lot of them are like that.
The publican is a tax collector, and Israel hated the tax collectors because they worked for Rome.

“God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are”. Not only does the Pharisee glorify himself in the sight of God, he puts down a brother next to him that is praying: even like this wicked publican, I ain’t like him. This is what Christ is talking about. “I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess.”

“The publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven”: that’s humility. He “smote upon his breast”, beat upon his breast, the way you do when you are weeping in sorrow over what you’ve done, the guilt and shame you have: “God be merciful to me a sinner.”

“This man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.” So we have to be mindful to keep a humble and meek attitude in this truth always, glory in the Lord, and not set ourselves up as better than one another.

precepts.why:
This is for the holier-than-thou. Brothers put on their fringes and the frenemies out there say, ‘you trying to be holier than thou for wearing fringes’. No, that’s the commandment of the Lord.

“I am sought of them that asked not for me”: that’s us. We did not ask for the Lord; we had no idea about a black God, a black savior, or that we are the children of Israel. All our lives we worshipped this white man and his idols. “I said, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name”: the nation not called by God’s name is African-American, Puerto Rican, Jamaican, Haitian, Brazilian.

“I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people”: we are the rebellious people, “which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts”. Those last four words: our people walk after their own thoughts. That’s the world we live in today. “That sacrificeth in gardens, and burneth incense upon altars of brick”: the little churches we set up, the same as the people worshipping under the trees in Papua New Guinea. “Which eat swine’s flesh, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels”: our people eat pork and all manner of unclean foods in these churches.

Here’s the point: “Which say, Stand by thyself, come not near to me; for I am holier than thou.” Get away from me, don’t bring that Bible over here: ‘I’m water baptized, Holy Ghost filled, washed in the blood of the Lamb.’ That’s them. It’s hard to say, but it’s nine out of ten black women doing that: I am so holy, and then turn out to be the biggest whores on the planet, sucking the deacon down. Growing up in church, me and my brother hiding in the basement, look what Pastor doing. So don’t talk about Christian churches; they make me want to vomit.

“These are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burneth all the day.” When you’ve got smoke in your nose you can’t stand it. God is saying, I can’t stand these people, they make me sick. That is the Pharisee of Luke 18:11, holier than the brother beside him.

The one who is so holy just had two abortions. “The Lord killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up.”

“The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich”. If you are poor right now, brothers and sisters, it’s the Lord that has done it. Not the one who dropped out of school and says the Lord did this to him: no, you did that to you. But if you went to school, got your education, met the right people, did all you could do and you’re still down and out, that’s the Lord’s hand on it. “He bringeth low, and lifteth up”: it is him that brings low and him that lifts up, the way Luke 18:14 says the one that exalts himself is abased and the one that humbles himself is exalted.

“He raiseth up the poor out of the dust”: that’s where we are coming to now. That dust is this ball of confusion. “And lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill”: we are the beggar, always asking for a handout. Can I have a job, can I have some money, can I have my own black woman. ‘Brother, I don’t live in a dunghill, I got a nice house.’ No, that’s a dunghill when you examine whence we came, ruling the planet, to this. Three mansions is a dunghill compared to what our forefathers and foremothers once had. What we have is crumbs, and it has become so normal to us.

“To set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory”: the Lord is going to set us among princes and make us inherit the throne of glory, rulership of the planet. “For the pillars of the earth are the Lord’s, and he hath set the world upon them.”

sense.text:
Back to what was read earlier. “Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom”: that’s for you educated brothers. “Neither let the mighty man glory in his might”: that’s for you big strong brothers. “Let not the rich man glory in his riches”: some of you have money, funds, resources, and it says don’t glory in your riches. Andrew Tate brags about his resources all the time.

Money is not unimportant, because the Bible does say money answers all things. But don’t glory in it.

precepts.why:
“For wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence”. Money is not being knocked, because the Bible says money is a defence. You need money to defend against utter poverty and against miseducation; if you want a good education you need money, and money to travel, to get food, to take care of yourself.

“But the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom giveth life to them that have it.” You need wisdom with your money. Some of you put your money in the stock market with no wisdom and lose it with the press of a button: damn, the stock market crashed. So the rich man of Jeremiah 9:23 is not to glory in riches, but he needs wisdom with them.

This is said first, before getting into some things about rich people: money is not unimportant. “A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all things.” In this world we do need money. What Jeremiah 9:23 forbids is glorying in it.

sense.text: Now we get into some things about rich people. Listen good: “The poor is hated even of his own neighbour”: everybody hates poor people. “But the rich hath many friends”: everybody loves a rich man, ’cause he has resources.

precepts.why:
“A rich man beginning to fall is held up of his friends”: when a rich man is about to fall, all his friends hold him up. Like Donald Trump: remember he went bankrupt, and everybody gave him loans when he filed for bankruptcy. I said, what the hell is this? I can’t get a loan. “But a poor man being down is thrust also away by his friends”: when you’re poor, even your friends push you away. Ah, we ain’t helping you, get out of here.

“When a rich man is fallen, he hath many helpers”: when a rich man falls he got everybody helping him. “He speaketh things not to be spoken”: he will speak things that should never be uttered, “and yet men justify him”: people will still justify him just because he’s rich. “The poor man slipped, and yet they rebuked him too”: they rebuke the poor brother. “He spake wisely, and could have no place”: the poor man spoke very wise, and there’s no place for him. Get out of here.

“When a rich man speaketh, every man holdeth his tongue”. Y’all remember that E.F. Hutton commercial: when E.F. Hutton speaks, everybody listens. He could be saying some dumb stuff and people’s listening to this dude. “And, look, what he saith, they extol it to the clouds”: whatever the rich man says, no matter how stupid or foul, they extol it to the clouds. “But if the poor man speak, they say, What fellow is this?”: if we speak, they say, who the hell is this? “And if he stumble, they will help to overthrow him.”

“Riches are good unto him that hath no sin”: riches are only good to him that have no sin. “And poverty is evil in the mouth of the ungodly”, because when you ungodly you will rob, you will steal, you will rape, you will do all manner of evil from there.

sense.text: “And he looked up, and saw the rich men casting their gifts into the treasury.” I’m going somewhere: I’m showing that these rich men the Bible’s talking about is first and foremost our people.

“This poor widow hath cast in more than they all: For all these have of their abundance cast in unto the offerings of God”: from all their abundance they gave a little bit. “But she of her penury hath cast in all the living that she had”: the little bit that she gave, that’s all she had. So Christ said she gave more than all of them.

precepts.why:
“Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you. Your riches are corrupted, and your garments are motheaten. Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you”, because they have not been dealing right. These rich brothers that James is talking about are Israelites, like we just read about, who have been foulmouthed, corrupt brothers. “And shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days.”

“Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth”: these same rich men will hire you, and they didn’t pay. They found every excuse not to pay the Israelites, their brothers: they working for you, but they going to hold back. They were defrauding the brothers. “And the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of the Lord of sabaoth.” Sabaoth means host: Lord of hosts. That’s not Sabbath.

“Ye have lived in pleasure on the earth, and been wanton”: these rich Israelites have lived in pleasure on the earth, lustful, sexing around. “Ye have nourished your hearts, as in a day of slaughter. Ye have condemned and killed the just”: these rich Israelites were against the followers of Christ. “And he doth not resist you.”

sense.text: Still talking about the rich. “Good Master, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?” Christ answers: “if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.” So the way to enter eternal life is keeping the commandments.

“Thou shalt do no murder, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness, Honour thy father and thy mother: and, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.” The young man says, “All these things have I kept from my youth up”: I’ve always kept those laws. “What lack I yet?”: what am I lacking?

“If thou wilt be perfect”: if you want to be perfect in the sight of God, “go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.” The ignorant thought is that Christ was saying give up everything and be homeless. No, that’s not what he’s saying. He’s saying help your brothers, help your people.
“But when the young man heard that saying, he went away sorrowful: for he had great possessions.” He had a lot, and he did not want to help his people.
“A rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven.” He didn’t say it’s impossible; he said hardly. It’s hard.

“It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.” That’s called the eye of the needle: a smaller gate to enter the castles or the walls of the city. At a certain time the main gate is closed, and in order for that man and the camel to get through that small gate, he has to unload the camel, bring everything, and the camel has to crawl in with his stuff. So it’s not impossible. It’s doable.

precepts.why: This is what Christ was telling them to do: they had all things common. “Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold”. Does that mean they sold everything and were homeless? No, that makes no sense. They had abundance.

“And all that believed were together, and had all things common; And sold their possessions and goods, and parted them to all men, as every man had need.” You see that: as every man had need. So this is what the young man did not want to do.

sense.text: “Hear this, all ye people; give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world: Both low and high, rich and poor, together.”
“I will incline mine ear to a parable: I will open my dark saying”: the dark sayings are parables, the same thing Christ spoke in.

“Wherefore should I fear in the days of evil, when the iniquity of my heels shall compass me about?” You ever hear that expression people say: all that evil you did, one day it’s going to catch up to you. That’s what that’s saying. The evil you’ve done will catch up to you eventually.

“They that trust in their wealth, and boast themselves in the multitude of their riches; None of them can by any means redeem his brother”: you can’t redeem your brother with it, “nor give to God a ransom for him.”

I went over this before, but I want to touch it again. “There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day”. In this parable it goes into some real stuff. The rich man is the rich man of Israel, like we read in James 5 and Matthew 19.

“And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus”. Lazarus represents the elect of our people, the poor. Remember what we read earlier in 1 Samuel 2: he will lift up the beggar from the dunghill. So Lazarus here is this beggar, “laid at his gate, full of sores”. And with Isaiah 1 we know that Lazarus here represents our people.

“And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table”: he wanted crumbs, he wanted a little handout. The rich man’s table is the chief priests and the Pharisees, and it goes perfectly with James 5: those rich men that held back your payment of labour by fraud. That’s what these people was doing.

“Moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.” The dogs are the other nations, and the wicked of our people as well. When it says the dogs licked his sores, they took advantage, like these other nations move into our communities and set up stores and all that.

“And it came to pass, that the beggar died”: he dropped dead, “and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom”: carried by the angels into the promise of Abraham. Abraham’s bosom, that’s going into the kingdom. “The rich man also died, and was buried”.

“And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.” This is crazy, because you get people, frenemies, that say when you die you die, that’s it. Now we know you die today, you at rest; we know that. But when Christ comes and opens that realm, ’cause them missiles going to hit, it’s going to be a lake of fire; yes, all that’s true. There will be a realm in there where you will not escape. You have done wickedness all your lives and you going to escape? Okay, that makes a lot of sense.

He saw Abraham far off in the distance, and Lazarus was enjoying the kingdom.
“Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.”

“Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things”: that’s what we just read in Esdras. You had benefits in this world. “And likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted”: Lazarus is comforted in the kingdom, “and thou art tormented”: you’re being tormented.

“Between us and you there is a great gulf fixed”: that’s what we read in Isaiah 66. “So that they which would pass from hence to you cannot”: that’s how you know it’s another realm. We will not be allowed to pass to them, “neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.”

“I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house: For I have five brethren”: five brothers, all womanizers, filthy rich, “that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.”

“They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.” This lets you know these are Israelites. They got Moses and the prophets. Esau did not have Moses and the prophets; Jacob had Moses and the prophets. So it’s talking about Israelites. And they had Moses and the prophets right there in their day, and they were still not going to listen to them.

“If one went unto them from the dead, they will repent.” “If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.” So there is no magic scripture. When Christ rose from the dead they still didn’t believe, and when he raised Lazarus, they plotted to kill Lazarus.

precepts.why: Full of sores: “From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores”. Look up in the chapter who it’s talking about. It is Israel, so when we go back to Luke 16:20, we know that Lazarus, full of sores, represents our people.

Verse 4 tells you who Isaiah 1:6 is talking about: “Ah sinful nation”. Verse 3: “The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master’s crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.” The one with the putrifying sores is Israel, our people, and that is the beggar Lazarus full of sores.

The rich man’s table is the scribes and Pharisees, and it goes perfectly with James 5: those rich men that held back the labourers’ pay by fraud. “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.”

Who gave them their place and nation? The Romans gave them theirs. Just like all of these politicians and these pastors: America gave them those seats of authority. America’s the one that chooses black leaders who’s going to do what we say. They got those positions from America. So it’s the same thing back during the time of Christ.

“Moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.” Now these dogs: “But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.” So the dogs in Exodus is making reference to the Egyptians.

“Then came she and worshipped him, saying, Lord, help me. But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.” It is not right to take the children’s bread, to take my healing power, and to cast it to dogs. So Christ called this woman of another nation a dog. So far we have the Egyptians in Exodus 11 and this woman here in Matthew 15.

Who’s this woman? The verse tells you her race: “behold, a woman of Canaan came out of the same coasts, and cried unto him, saying, Have mercy on me, O Lord, thou Son of David”. She is of another nation, and that is the woman Christ calls a dog.

“His watchmen are blind: they are all ignorant, they are all dumb dogs”. That includes our people too: God is calling them dumb dogs, ’cause the white man set some of our people up as watchmen along with other nations. “They cannot bark”: they cannot warn the people of danger, “sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber. Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough”.

Like what we showed today with the brother Billy Carson: you would be considered a dog, because you’re reaping financial gain from a poor and destitute people and you’re not helping us at all; you’re just giving us lies after lies after lies. So the dogs that licked Lazarus’s sores are the other nations and the wicked of our people as well.

Mark tells the same account as Matthew 15: “The woman was a Greek”. “But Jesus said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it unto the dogs.” So you got the Egyptians in Exodus 11, you got the woman from Canaan in Matthew 15, a Greek in Mark 7: the dogs are the other nations.

Now don’t get mad, get glad. “And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord.” The whole planet is going to be forced to observe the new moon holiday and the Sabbath; everybody’s going to be made to obey.

“And they shall go forth”: that’s the righteous shall go forth, “and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die”: their worm, that’s about their soul; it shall not die. “Neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.” You see those people over there screaming, those rebellious ones against the Lord? Everybody is going to see them spirits.

Y’all keep playing. You got camps telling you you can eat pork and it’s good in Yahawashi; that ain’t gonna work, and bragging about it. You got camps saying you could buy prostitutes and it’s good in Yahawashi. Y’all keep being fooled by these people out here.

“And if thy hand offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched”. Now you telling me nothing’s going to happen when you die? You a liar, brother; I’m reading it.

What it means to cut off the hand that offends you: “If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, thou, nor thy fathers; Namely, of the gods of the people which are round about you, nigh unto thee, or far off from thee, from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth”. What we going to do? “Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him; neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, neither shalt thou conceal him: But thou shalt surely kill him”. “Then shall they be in pitiful case, which now have abused my ways”: which now have abused God’s way, his laws. You got the Bible but you’re doing wrong with the understanding; you manipulate the people. “And they that have cast them away despitefully shall dwell in torments”: you’re going to live in torments. Keep playing.

“For such as in their life have received benefits”, like the rich man we reading about, “and have not known me; And they that have lothed my law”, they that hated God’s law, “while they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it”: they despised repentance. There’s no contradiction: they shall look upon them, and between us and them is a gulf no one can pass.

Though one rose from the dead, they would not be persuaded. We got to put that dude back to death? The hell is this.

Remember what Abraham told the rich man: they got Moses and the prophets, and if they won’t hear them, they won’t hear one risen from the dead. sense.text:
“If any man worship the beast”: write this down, that’s Edom, Edom particularly America. “And his image”: what is his image? That’s Revelation 13.

“If any man worship the beast”: what sin is that? Idolatry. Remember this last sin. The first sin was idolatry, and God is saying the last thing is going to be idolatry too.

“And receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand”: a mark identifies you; that’s how you know if you worship this beast. The mark is sin. Your forehead is your mind: you believe in sin. And you support the sin with your hand: you do it.

“The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb”. That’s how you know this is going to be another realm, a spirit realm that you will suffer in. That’s what this is talking about.

“And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night”. This is what the parable Christ gave about Lazarus and the rich man is. “Who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name”: you receive that sin mark.

Now how do we escape that? Verse 12 is how we escape. “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.” That is the solution to all that we just read.

precepts.why:
What is his image? Worship this white man and his image. “And he doeth great wonders, so that he maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men”: that was the atom bomb, nuclear destruction. Could it happen again? Yes it can. It happened before, and what we’re reading here can, and very well may, happen again here in this country.

“And deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by the means of those miracles”: notice what caused that destructive fire, miracles. “Which he had power to do in the sight of the beast”: that beast there is the European powers, Edom. “Saying to them that dwell on the earth, that they should make an image to the beast”: that they should make an image to the white man, “which had the wound by a sword, and did live.” That’s talking about Rome. Rome was the nation that had a wound by the sword: they fell, then resurrected during the Renaissance; they came back. So this image would be in honor of Rome, that’s Caesar.

This is how deep it goes, with that AI Jesus; y’all keep playing. “And he had power to give life unto the image of the beast”: they gave that image the life of Christ; they say that’s Jesus. “That the image of the beast should both speak, and cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed.” We are coming to a crucial point in time. Just keep your eyes open; all I can do is warn you.

People often ask how come Revelation seems so different from the other books in the New Testament. It’s not; it’s saying the same thing. “Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God”: this is what we read in Revelation 13. “Or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God.” That’s the white man, the Roman Catholic Church. It’s all in there; that’s what they do, show themselves that they are God. Once you understand the scriptures you will not be deceived.

If any man worship the beast: what sin is that? Idolatry. “For the worshipping of idols not to be named is the beginning, the cause, and the end, of all evil.” So the first sin was idolatry, and God is saying the last thing is going to be idolatry too. This is what we’re reading in Revelation 14.

“Receive his mark”: a mark identifies you. How do you know if you worship this beast? Let’s see what the mark is. “If I sin, then thou markest me”: that’s the mark. Sin is the mark.

Following this idolatrous religion is sin. Y’all are seeing these sins creeping into society, the LGBT, and if you don’t accept it and use the proper pronouns you get fired, you get terminated, kicked out of school. It’s slowly but surely creeping in, and people are slowly but surely accepting it and condemning us for saying no, that goes against the Bible, that goes against the word of God. They get mad at us.

sense.text: “For there shall be in every place, and in the next cities, a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord.” Those of us who stand devoted to this Bible: there’s going to be an insurrection against us. We’re going against the status quo. Remember in the Solomon Islands they said you guys are against the Catholic Church, you’re against all religions. Yeah, God is too. They made us public enemy number one.
“They shall be like mad men, sparing none”: those of our people that get caught, they’re not going to spare us. “But still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord.” This is the prophecy.
“For they shall waste and take away their goods”: the goods of you brothers and sisters with nice homes and houses. “And cast them out of their houses”: you’re going to be cast out of your houses.

“Then shall they be known, who are my chosen”: that’s how we’re going to know who the chosen are, those that endure. Christ said he that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved. We’ve got to endure this. “And they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.”

“Behold, the days of trouble are at hand”: that’s Jacob’s trouble. “But I will deliver you from the same.” What do you mean, when it just said in the verses above that we’re going to be put to death? The righteous never die. Understand that.

“Be ye not afraid”: don’t be afraid of what’s to come. “Neither doubt”: when trouble and tribulation come upon us, don’t fear, don’t doubt, because the two are synonymous. “For God is your guide”: he’s already told us what’s going to happen. So when it’s happening to certain of us, don’t be shocked, don’t be amazed, asking why is this happening to me. You know the scriptures: study to show yourself approved. Faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. Constantly meditate on what is to come, so that you can prepare yourself.

“Let not your sins weigh you down”: whatever sins you’re involved in, don’t let them weigh you down; repent and keep it moving. “And let not your iniquities lift up themselves”: don’t play with your sins. They will rise up in you and take over.

“Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins”, because you let your iniquities rise up in you. Once again you went back to the alcoholism, you went back to the weed. That’s what you did. “And covered with their iniquities, like as a field is covered over with bushes, and the path thereof covered with thorns, that no man may travel through”: nobody can help you. There’s no scripture that can reach you, because you’re covered with your sins; you’re overcome with sin.

“It is left undressed, and is cast into the fire to be consumed therewith.” That’s the same fire we’ve been reading about, the same fire Christ has been warning us about, the same fire of Revelation 14, the fire some of these Israelites say ain’t going to happen.

precepts.why: God said “I will deliver you from the same”, though the verses above say we’re going to be put to death. The righteous never die. “Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord”: y’all hear that? Blessed are the dead that die in the Lord, that die in his truth. “From henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours”: that you may rest from your labours; the Bible says blessed are you. “And their works do follow them”: the works that you’ve done shall follow you.

sense.text:
What we read in Revelation is saying the same thing here. Many of the books and chapters say pretty much the same thing; they’re just using different words.

“Art not thou it that remainest of the four beasts”: the fourth beast is Rome, which is the United States of America. America is an extension of Rome. We are living in the fourth beast. Notice what it says: “whom I made to reign in my world”. Remember Babylon: Daniel warned Nebuchadnezzar about his pride. God allowed you to reign.

“That the end of their times might come through them”: God had this white man create such weapons that they’re going to destroy themselves. It’s going to bring about the end of their world. Armageddon is the end of their world.

“And the fourth came”: that’s Rome, America. “And overcame all the beasts that were past, and had power over the world with great fearfulness”: just like Rome had power over the world, America today has power over the world. “And over the whole compass of the earth with much wicked oppression”: it’s America bringing forth much wicked oppression. “And so long time dwelt he upon the earth with deceit”: with lies.
“For the earth hast thou not judged with truth.” Rome did not judge the world with truth.

“For thou hast afflicted the meek, thou hast hurt the peaceable”: this part right here is how you know it gets into America. You hurt the ten tribes. That’s America: Spain, Portugal and them, then they formed themselves the United States of America.

“Thou hast loved liars”: that’s the politicians. “And destroyed the dwellings of them that brought forth fruit”: you destroyed the American Indians, you destroyed the so-called Mexicans, you destroyed them. “And hast cast down the walls of such as did thee no harm.”

“Therefore is thy wrongful dealing come up unto the Highest”: so you thought the Lord didn’t see and acknowledge the evil you did to the tribes of Israel. “And thy pride unto the Mighty”: the same pride Babylon had is the same pride they have today.

“The Highest also hath looked upon the proud times”: their proud times are their technology. They said we are all powerful, we are God. “And, behold, they are ended”: God says your proud times are ended, your technology is ended. “And his abominations are fulfilled”: your abominations are fulfilled.

“And therefore appear no more, thou eagle”: that’s giving you the symbol of the last country on earth. The United States of America’s symbol is that fourth beast: the eagle. Christians say we don’t know what the fourth symbol is. The Bible tells you; if they didn’t snatch it out of the original King James Version you would have known something.

“Nor thy horrible wings, nor thy wicked feathers”. “Nor thy malicious heads”: their leaders, wicked heads. “Nor thy hurtful claws”: that’s their military. “Nor all thy vain body”: that’s their citizens.

“That all the earth may be refreshed”: when this country goes down, all the earth may be refreshed. “And may return, being delivered from thy violence, and that she may hope for the judgment and mercy of him that made her.”

precepts.why:
They made weapons to destroy themselves; that’s what Esdras is saying. “Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire”: the smith is called a scientist today. “And that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster”: that’s the ICBM, new nuclear weaponry, “to destroy.”

So these weapons: God had this man learn that technology, “that the end of their times might come through them.” They’re going to destroy themselves.

We just read “thou hast hurt the peaceable”. Who are the peaceable? “And whereas thou sawest that he gathered another peaceable multitude unto him; Those are the ten tribes”, the ten tribes of Israel, “which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.” So the ten tribes were taken to the Assyrian in captivity.

“But they took this counsel among themselves”: when Persia came into power, the ten tribes took counsel among themselves, “that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt, That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.” “For the most High then shewed signs for them, and held still the flood, till they were passed over. For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half: and the same region is called Arsareth.”

Look up Arsareth: the name of the land beyond the great river, far away from the habitation of man, in which the ten tribes of Israel would dwell observing the laws of Moses until the time of restoration, according to Fourth Ezra 13. It says Fourth Ezra because of how the books of Ezra are counted; it’s the one we call second Esdras. Columbus identified America with this land.

So go back to 2 Esdras 11:42: “thou hast hurt the peaceable”. You hurt the ten tribes. That’s America.
